source.title: Robust Neural Network Training using Periodic Sampling over Model Weights
source.authors: S. Tripathi; Jiayi Liu; Sauptik Dhar; U. Kurup; Mohak Shah

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including supplementary material. Its title differs from the provided TITLE: the paper text is titled “Improving Model Training by Periodic Sampling over Weight Distributions.”
record.tranche_reason: Applies periodic weight sampling and momentum during training in image-classification and vision tasks, then reports held-out performance and training stability.
record.gate_note: The study does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, optimizer rankings, batch-size effects, or dropout. Its loss-surface analysis reports wider minima but does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or rank generalization gaps. Cited findings are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates periodic weight sampling, not any listed claim version. Its filter-normalized loss landscapes do not test whether magnitude-aware sharpness tracks or ranks generalization gaps (V7). Adam's poorer generalization is cited rather than established by an Adam-versus-SGD experiment (V4).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that periodic weight sampling improves stability, intermediate performance, and convergence speed. PWALKS and PSWM address PSWA's failure to reach optimal final performance on deeper networks; PSWA itself does not consistently preserve optimal convergence.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces periodic weight averaging, averaging over the last batches, and momentum-based weight updates; it does not reproduce any of the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with method (PSWA, PWALKS, PSWM), network depth, learning rate, training stage, and optimizer. The paper says PSWA fails to converge optimally for deeper networks but works on shallow networks; PWALKS and PSWM address that issue.

fits_no_version.finding: On ImageNet ResNet50, weight-sampling methods improve average intermediate accuracy and reduce accuracy variability across epochs. Final-period mean accuracy is lower for PSWA, higher for PWALKS, and equal for PSWM relative to SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Periodic weight sampling can improve intermediate held-out performance and training stability, with final performance depending on the sampling method.

fits_no_version.finding: For CIFAR-10 ResNet18, PSWA produces wider filter-normalized loss landscapes than SGD, including at convergence when train and test accuracies are similar.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Periodic weight averaging can widen local loss landscapes without a corresponding improvement in train or test accuracy.

record.peer_reviewed: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (Big Data)
record.problems: The loss-surface comparison is figure-only and has no reported numeric sharpness or gap-ranking measure. Tables report aggregate improvements and standard deviations without confidence intervals or significance tests. Some results are described only in figures, and supplementary experiments are referenced without numeric values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results were left out. Figure-based comparisons for training thresholds, other datasets, and other tasks are not tabulated numerically in the supplied text and do not test a listed version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning conditions; recovery through broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Dropout effects, small-data regimes, excessive dropout, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Whether magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance tracks generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks and ranks them better than norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T3 classification and V7 tested_not_extracted status should be corrected. Different batch sizes across datasets are not a controlled batch-size experiment. R1–R5 are method-performance comparisons outside the listed versions; retain them only as contextual findings.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width sweep beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD generalization under tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
The paper compares loss-surface widths but does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or test how well that measure ranks generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
